root_cause.text: A time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in sched_ext cgroup setter functions (scx_group_set_{weight,idle,bandwidth}) where the `scx_root` pointer is read without holding the `scx_cgroup_ops_rwsem` lock, allowing a concurrent scheduler unload to free the pointed-to structure and then a new scheduler load to change `scx_root`, leading to use-after-free when the stale pointer is later dereferenced under the lock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "scx_group_set_{weight,idle,bandwidth}() cache scx_root before acquiring scx_cgroup_ops_rwsem, so the pointer can be stale by the time the op runs. If the loaded scheduler is disabled and freed (via RCU work) and another is enabled between the naked load and the rwsem acquire, the reader sees scx_cgroup_enabled=true (the new scheduler's) but dereferences the freed one - UAF on SCX_HAS_OP(sch, ...) / SCX_CALL_OP(sch, ...)." The patch moves `sch = scx_root;` inside the `percpu_down_read(&scx_cgroup_ops_rwsem);` critical section for each affected function.

Author: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed May 14 11:11:48 2025 -0400

    sched_ext: Clean up scx_root usages
    
    - Always cache scx_root into local variable sch before using.
    
    - Don't use scx_root if cached sch is available.
    
    - Wrap !sch test with unlikely().
    
    - Pass @scx into scx_cgroup_init/exit().
    
    No behavior changes intended.
    
    Signed-off-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
    Reviewed-by: Andrea Rig
bic_trace_step.reason: In scx_group_set_weight(), the local variable sch is assigned from scx_root before taking the scx_cgroup_rwsem lock (line 4154: 'struct scx_sched *sch = scx_root;' before 'percpu_down_read(&scx_cgroup_rwsem);' at line 4156). This read of scx_root without holding the lock creates a TOCTOU race condition, as a concurrent scheduler unload could free the structure and a subsequent load could change scx_root, leading to use-after-free. The commit does not add any locking or other fix, so the vulnerable construct remains.
